title: The Fruit of the Spirit
lead: The nine qualities Paul lists in Galatians 5:22-23 as what the Spirit grows in believers: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control. He sets them against the works of the flesh and says no law stands against them.

sections.b: Paul does not say 'works of the Spirit.' The flesh produces many scattered works, and the Spirit one fruit, which is grown and not made. The list is often grouped in threes. It is set against the works of the flesh in Galatians 5:19-21 and is aimed at a church that was biting and devouring itself. The fruit image comes from the Old Testament (Isaiah 5; Psalm 1:3) and from Jesus (Matthew 7:16-20; John 15:1-8). Other lists of Spirit-given qualities appear in Ephesians 5:9 and Colossians 3:12-15.
sections.refs: Galatians 5:19-23; Psalm 1:3; Matthew 7:16-20; John 15:1-8; Ephesians 5:9; Colossians 3:12-15

sections.b: The fruit of the Spirit is not the same as the gifts of the Spirit (1 Corinthians 12-14). Gifts are given to some for service; the fruit is meant for every believer. Paul puts love, the first fruit, above all gifts in 1 Corinthians 13.
